language.script_notes: Distinctive vocabulary/slang, though signage vocabulary is broadly standard Latin American Spanish. Street suffixes: Calle, Avenida, Pasaje, Camino.
false_friends: Argentina (shares much of the Andes border)

road_furniture.bollard_color: Yellow reflective panels on bollards and guardrails — a fairly reliable Chile tell.
road_furniture.bollard_shape: Varies; often paired with grooved sign poles that resemble telephone poles.
road_furniture.guardrail_type: Standard steel guardrail with yellow reflectors as noted above.
road_furniture.line_paint: All four combinations (white/yellow outside and inside) are seen depending on road type.
road_furniture.curb_style: Painted kerbs in cities; minimal shoulders on remote desert/mountain roads.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Terpel, COPEC, Petrobras and ENEX are common fuel-station brands. No border/background panel behind speed-limit numbers is a subtle Chile tell shared with Spain.

architecture.roof_style: Varies enormously by region given the country's extreme north-south length — flat-roofed desert buildings in the north, French-influenced pitched-roof wine estates in the center, and Alpine-style lodges further south. See regional profiles.
architecture.wall_construction: Highly regional — see North/Central/Patagonia profiles for specifics.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Colourful hillside houses in Valparaíso; French-inspired 19th-century wine estates in the Central Valley; stark mining infrastructure in the northern desert; Alpine-style lodges and estancias in the south.

nature.vegetation: Extraordinarily varied given the country's 4,300km north-south length — the hyper-arid, nearly vegetation-free Atacama Desert in the north, Mediterranean vineyards and farmland in the Central Valley, and temperate rainforest, fjords and glaciers in the south. See regional profiles.
nature.terrain: A narrow strip squeezed between the Pacific Ocean and the Andes for its entire length — the driest non-polar desert on Earth in the north, fertile central valley, and a fjord-and-glacier-carved southern coast.
nature.climate_signature: Climate changes dramatically by latitude — desert in the north, Mediterranean in the center, cold and wet in Patagonia. Chile's extreme length makes regional identification essential.

vehicles.plate_color: White plate with black text; taxi plates can be orange, red, white or green depending on type.
vehicles.plate_format: AB CD 12 (two letters, two letters, two digits).
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Standard mixed Latin American fleet; mining trucks common in the northern desert.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mixed Gen 3/4; part of Chile's coverage is recognizable by showing the white rear of the Google car.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Dense around Santiago and the Central Valley; progressively sparser moving into the Atacama and Patagonia.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shares the Andes mountain border for nearly the entire length of both countries, overlapping Patagonian terrain in the far south
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Chile sits on the Pacific (wetter, western) side of the Andes with a white-rear Google car look in parts; Argentina sits on the drier eastern steppe side with its own black-car Gen 3 coverage — Chile is also a much narrower north-south strip than Argentina's broader territory.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Atacama-adjacent desert coastline and Pacific-side geography in the north
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Chile's yellow-reflector bollards and plate format differ from Peru's; Peruvian architecture and Andean cultural presence (Quechua influence) is generally more visible than in northern Chile.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Andean altiplano terrain and border region in the north
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Bolivia is landlocked with a much larger Indigenous Andean cultural presence visible in architecture and dress; Chile's Pacific coastline and national road furniture differ once compared directly.
